name: Mesterolone

card.summary: Proviron: a mild oral DHT derivative used in medicine for male hypogonadism and fertility, and by forum users as an add-on for hardness and libido; appearance effects are untested.
card.note: Fertility trials are mixed; forum reports describe small or no physique effects.

quick.overview:
Mesterolone, best known as Proviron, is an oral androgen derived from dihydrotestosterone. Clinically it has been used for male hypogonadism and was tested for male infertility. On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a mild add-on to testosterone for libido, a drier look, and, among younger users, as a way to raise DHT, sometimes under the label of puberty maxxing.

No published study has examined mesterolone for muscle, facial or skin appearance. The fertility trials give mixed results, and the one detailed forum self-report on looksmax.org described only small changes.
quick.mechanism: Mesterolone is a 1-alpha-methyl derivative of DHT that acts on the androgen receptor and is not aromatized to estrogen; Grokipedia reports high binding to sex-hormone-binding globulin, which forum users cite as the reason it is added to stacks.[1][2]
quick.risks: Grokipedia describes a low risk of liver toxicity relative to other oral androgens, but safety data in healthy users are limited to forum reports.[1] Users raise DHT-related concerns such as hair loss and discuss whether use suppresses the natural hormonal axis; a 1974 study measured pituitary-testicular function in normal men.[3][4][5] It is prohibited in sport.

lead: Mesterolone (brand name Proviron) is a synthetic oral androgen derived from dihydrotestosterone with a methyl group at the 1-alpha position. Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, describes it as strongly androgenic and weakly anabolic, not aromatizable to estrogen, and associated with a low risk of liver toxicity.[1]

In medicine it has been used for androgen deficiency in men and was trialled for idiopathic male infertility, with inconsistent results: a randomized trial in 40 subfertile men reported higher semen volume and sperm concentration on mesterolone than on placebo, while a separate randomized comparison of six months' treatment found no significant increase in sperm concentration or partner pregnancies.[6][7] A Cochrane review of androgens for idiopathic oligo/asthenospermia examined mesterolone and testosterone undecanoate among other agents.[8][9]

On looksmax.org, Proviron is discussed as a mild add-on, a way to raise DHT, and a supposed safe compound for younger users; community opinion is divided. One user's documented trial of Proviron alone reported stronger erections and a slightly drier look with no change in strength or muscle mass.[2][10][11]
infobox: Prescription drug in many countries; prohibited in sport

paras: Mesterolone has been used as androgen replacement in hypogonadal men. A double-blind randomized comparison of testosterone undecanoate and mesterolone in 26 hypogonadal men assessed effects on sexual activity and mental state.[12] Reviews of hypogonadism therapy discuss alternatives to testosterone, and studies of various androgen substitution regimens examined effects on erythropoiesis, lipids, bone and prostate.[13][14][15][16][17] A trial in normal men examined mesterolone's effect on pituitary-testicular function.[5]

For infertility, a 1987 randomized trial gave mesterolone or placebo to 40 men with idiopathic oligospermia for over four months and found significant increases in semen volume, mean sperm concentration and total sperm count, with motility and morphology unchanged.[6] A 1983 randomized comparison of placebo, clomiphene, mesterolone, pentoxifylline and testosterone enanthate in 46 men found that placebo, mesterolone, pentoxifylline and testosterone rebound therapy did not significantly increase sperm concentration or partner pregnancy.[7] A placebo-controlled trial of high-dose mesterolone in idiopathic infertility was published in 1991, and reviews of male infertility treatment describe pharmacological therapy as largely empirical.[18][19] A Cochrane review on androgens for idiopathic oligo/asthenospermia was later withdrawn.[9][8]

Looksmaxxing users describe mesterolone as an add-on to testosterone for libido and to raise DHT. Threads ask whether it is useful at 15 or 17, whether it affects height or hair, whether it suppresses the hormonal axis, and whether an injectable form is sensible.[20][21][22][4][23] One post calls it the most underrated and safest compound for puberty-maxxing, while another titled a documented trial of Proviron alone as showing it is mostly cope.[10][2] No controlled study supports or refutes these cosmetic claims.

Clinical studies include randomized trials in idiopathic oligospermia (a 1987 placebo-controlled trial in 40 men, a 1983 six-month comparison in 46 men and a 1991 high-dose placebo-controlled trial), a randomized comparison with testosterone undecanoate in 26 hypogonadal men, and a study in normal men of pituitary-testicular function.[6][7][18][12][5] None assessed physique or appearance.

The user who documented a trial of Proviron alone reported stronger erections, better mood, a slightly drier look and slightly more vascularity, but no increase in muscle hardness, strength or mass and no effect on hair; he suggested it might help with sexual side effects from SSRIs, finasteride or deca.[2] A reply described it as very weak and mainly used alongside other steroids.[2] These are individual reports, not controlled data.
In published trials the clinically measured outcomes were sexual activity, mood and semen parameters rather than muscle or appearance.[12][6][7]

Published safety data specific to mesterolone in healthy users are scarce. Grokipedia lists virilization in women, prostatic effects, fluid retention and contraindication in pregnancy.[1] Forum users ask whether short courses suppress the hormonal axis, and one thread asks how DHT-raising compounds interact with finasteride and topical minoxidil for hair.[4][3] In that exchange a reply said inhibiting 5-alpha-reductase would do nothing against an already-formed DHT derivative, and that discontinuing finasteride would simply stop its protection.[3]

Urinary metabolites of mesterolone have been characterised by mass spectrometry for doping control, including long-term metabolites and markers in the sulfate fraction.[24][25] A relative-binding study of anabolic steroids examined androgen-receptor binding in muscle and prostate and sex-hormone-binding globulin binding.[26] Grokipedia reports that mesterolone binds SHBG about four times as strongly as DHT, which is the basis of the claim that it raises free testosterone; it states that this use lacks large clinical trials.[1]

Proviron is one of the more commonly mentioned adjunct compounds on looksmax.org; one thread asks why it is not discussed more, another is a megathread on benefits and side effects, and others ask where to source it.[11][27][28] Users also pair it with other compounds in teen cycle plans.[29][30]

timeline.event: A clinical report on mesterolone in the treatment of male infertility is published.[31]
A randomized comparison of mesterolone with placebo and other agents in idiopathic oligospermia finds no significant benefit.[7]
A randomized trial reports increased sperm counts in oligospermic men on mesterolone.[6]
A placebo-controlled trial of high-dose mesterolone in idiopathic male infertility is published.[18]

lore.intro: Proviron is discussed on looksmax.org as a mild, DHT-raising add-on, with some users calling it underrated and others calling it mostly ineffective.[10][2][11]

claims.claim: Proviron raises DHT and aids puberty-maxxing.
claims.believers: Users describe it as an underrated and safe compound for younger people wanting more DHT effect.[10][20]
claims.experts: No published study has examined mesterolone in adolescents for appearance outcomes; medical trials were in adult men.[12][6]

claims.claim: Proviron alone does little for muscle, hair or hardness.
claims.believers: One documented solo trial reported small changes in erections, mood and dryness and none in strength or muscle; replies called it very weak.[2]
claims.experts: Published trials measured sexual activity, mood and sperm parameters and did not measure physique.[12][6]

claims.claim: It improves sperm count and fertility.
claims.believers: A 1984 review notes that drug treatment of male infertility has been largely empirical, and mesterolone was one of the hormonal agents tried.[19]
claims.experts: One randomized trial found improved sperm counts, another found no significant effect on sperm concentration or pregnancy, and a Cochrane review of androgens for idiopathic oligo/asthenospermia was withdrawn.[6][7][9]

claims.claim: Raising DHT with Proviron will undo finasteride or increase hair loss.
claims.believers: Forum users ask whether stopping Proviron would cause loss of hair gains, and others say a DHT derivative bypasses 5-alpha-reductase inhibition.[3]
claims.experts: No study was found testing mesterolone against hair outcomes.[1]

claims.claim: It helps with sexual side effects of other drugs.
claims.believers: One user suggested it for erectile problems induced by SSRIs, finasteride or deca.[2]
claims.experts: A randomized comparison with testosterone undecanoate in hypogonadal men measured sexual activity and mental state, but not in drug-induced dysfunction.[12]
